speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin my evaluation, could you describe the specific nature of the pain and swelling in your right knee, and how long has this been occurring? Additionally, do you notice any specific triggers or patterns with your episodes of pain during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and recent sexual activity with multiple partners is highly suggestive of this condition, which often follows a genitourinary infection.
